clue.text: When top-of-the-range programmes are shown?

parts.note: top-of-the-range suggests the best shows, but the phrase is read as the hours of the evening when the largest audience watches television

explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters schedule their most popular shows for the evening slot when the most people are watching.

clue.text: Maybe I will leave sapphire off

indicators.note: the letter I is to go from the jewel's letters before they are rearranged
off signals that the remaining letters of the jewel are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is wondering whether to take off a sapphire ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will leave' takes I out of SAPPHIRE, giving SAPPHRE, and 'off' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express possibility without certainty, as synonyms.

clue.text: Reckoned total, and in eluded an extra 500

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Reckoned total, and in eluded an extra 500' is an OCR garble (perhaps 'included'); no parse of the wordplay to ADDED is evident and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Reckoned total, and in eluded an extra 500

clue.text: Vehicle taking shielded uranium into Pacific city

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: into means the uranium symbol is placed inside the word for shielded

parts.note: to cover is to shield, so shielded gives cover in the sense of a protective layer
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A truck carrying protected nuclear material is driven into a city on the Pacific coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just joins the vehicle to what follows; 'into' is the container signal, giving COUVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is the large Canadian port city on the Pacific coast of British Columbia.

clue.text: Gale finally behind ship from one quarter

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word Gale

parts.note: astern means behind or at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A strong wind picks up at the stern of a vessel from one direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern means coming from the east, one of the four quarters or compass directions.

clue.text: A moment for business this month

explanation.surface: A quick word about a business letter dated this month.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a very brief moment of time; in old business letters inst. abbreviates instant, meaning of the current month.

clue.text: Interrogate cook

explanation.definitionFit: To grill a suspect is to question them intensely; to grill food is to cook it under direct heat.

clue.text: Where shipwright may be accused

explanation.definitionFit: A dock is where ships are built or repaired, so a shipwright works there; the dock is also the courtroom enclosure where a defendant stands trial.

clue.text: From our planet? No such chance

explanation.definitionFit: Earthly means belonging to the world we live on; in 'not an earthly' or 'no earthly chance' it stresses that there is no possibility at all.

clue.text: Given overdose, in tears-rats!

indicators.note: in means the overdose abbreviation is placed inside the word for tears

parts.note: rents are tears or rips in cloth

explanation.surface: Someone who has taken an overdose is weeping and cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests crying but means rips; 'rats!' looks like an exclamation but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are gnawing animals belonging to the order of rodents, so they are examples.

clue.text: One that cuts money artist's model gets

indicators.note: gets means the artist's model takes in the money letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a sitter poses for an artist
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone who cuts a sitter's fee is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: A slitter is a person or machine that makes long narrow cuts, as in paper or metal.

clue.text: Stars man adored to distraction

indicators.note: driven to distraction means thrown into confusion, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man is madly in love, adoring someone to distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to distraction' rearranges the letters of MAN ADORED.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars, also containing a famous galaxy.

clue.text: A sucker for old-style medicine

explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm; in archaic English the word also meant a physician, hence old-style medicine.

clue.text: Had tried hard to find way to get rent

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
riven means torn apart, the same as rent as a past participle

explanation.surface: A tenant struggled to find a way to pay the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for a home but is the past participle of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Striven is the past participle of strive, so 'had striven' means made great efforts.

clue.text: Be frightened to break sacred urn

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it to pieces, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous about smashing a holy vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To run scared is an idiom for acting in panic out of fear.

clue.text: Hot-pot topping?

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew with a potato crust, but here it is read as a pot of hot tea and the padded cover put on it

explanation.definitionFit: A padded cover placed over a teapot keeps the brew warm.

clue.text: Flashy way of sending Morse

parts.note: flashy suggests showy, but it means using flashes of light to signal in Morse code, as ships do

explanation.definitionFit: This signalling lantern, named after its inventor Arthur Aldis, sends Morse code by flashes of light.

clue.text: One pitted against a goddess

parts.note: a miner works in a pit, so is one pitted
v is the abbreviation for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Someone is matched against a goddess in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitted against' looks like one phrase meaning opposed, but splits into a pit worker and V.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom and crafts.

clue.text: Car's quiet, at least

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a car runs quietly, at least.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, minimum means at the lowest, as in 'it costs ten pounds minimum'.

clue.text: Calf twice fails to start on a fodder plant

indicators.note: twice means the shortened word is written two times over
fails to start means the opening letter of the word Calf is dropped

explanation.surface: A young animal repeatedly refuses its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to start' drops C from CALF, giving ALF, which 'twice' doubles, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa, also called lucerne, is a clover-like crop grown to feed livestock.

clue.text: Has on some kinky leather

parts.note: to have someone on is to tease them, to kid them

indicators.note: some means only part of the word kinky is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is wearing kinky leather clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has on' looks like wearing but means teases.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidskin is soft leather made from the hide of a young goat.

clue.text: Here in Ireland larked about

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for Ireland goes inside the rearranged letters
about signals that the letters of larked are jumbled around

parts.note: I is a standard abbreviation for Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone had fun playing around while in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LARKED to KLDARE, and 'in' puts I inside it. The definition 'Here' works because the clue locates this place in Ireland: Kildare is an Irish county and town.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue frames this Irish county and town as the place being described, the spot where the larking happened.

clue.text: Wrote symbolically "Isn't a 1950s delinquent"

parts.note: isn't contains the negative not
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a young British rebel of the 1950s in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: Someone writes in code that a person is not a 1950s hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth known for drape jackets and rowdy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set down music or data in a system of signs.

clue.text: Coming out of shell is the making of Pearl

definitions.text: Coming out of shell is the making of Pearl

parts.words: Coming out of shell is the making of Pearl
parts.note: reads like a shy girl called Pearl gaining confidence, but describes the lustrous substance a mollusc secretes that builds up into a pearl

explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is the iridescent lining secreted by molluscs, layers of which form a pearl.

clue.text: Praise as old tax is reduced by one pound

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: is reduced by means one letter standing for a pound is taken away

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax for using a road or bridge
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: An outdated levy is cut by a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reduced by' removes one L from EXTOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to speak highly of, to laud.

clue.text: Too close to ground for parachute jump? Don't make it

definitions.text: Too close to ground for parachute jump?

explanation.definitionFit: A drop from too low a height would land before the canopy opened, a jump that fell short; to fall short is also to fail to reach a target.

clue.text: Make speech, and spit? Expect not

indicators.note: not means the letters of the word Expect are removed from the longer word

parts.note: to expectorate is to spit

explanation.surface: A speaker asks whether spitting is permitted and is told not to expect it.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address in a pompous way.

clue.text: Maiden not universal in a ceremony of marriage

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: not means the universal letter is left out of the ceremony word

parts.note: a ritual is a formal ceremony
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A bride takes part in a wedding rite.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M. 'not' removes U from RITUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to wedlock or the relationship between spouses.

clue.text: Inflexible man goes into fudged data

indicators.note: goes into means the word man is placed inside the jumbled letters
fudged figures have been tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stubborn man works on falsified data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fudged' gives ADAT; 'man' looks like the subject of the sentence but is fodder placed by 'goes into'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unwilling to change one's mind, as unyielding as hard stone.

clue.text: Unwelcome sign of growth in one's maturity?

definitions.text: Unwelcome sign of growth in one's maturity?

parts.words: Unwelcome sign of growth in one's maturity?
parts.note: growth in maturity suggests becoming wiser, but here means a thickening waistline as a person gets older

explanation.definitionFit: Extra fat around the waist often appears in people's forties and fifties.
